findings.title: retryCount deletion branch is not scoped to SMS method
findings.body: The new OR clause `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in the deleteMany call has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the sibling condition. The function is documented/intended to operate only on SMS reminders, but as written it will delete ANY WorkflowReminder row (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, SMS) whose retryCount happens to exceed 1, regardless of method. Since `retryCount` is a shared column on the WorkflowReminder model (not SMS-specific), any future code path that increments retryCount for non-SMS reminders (or any data migration/bug that sets retryCount>1) will cause this cron job to silently delete unrelated email/whatsapp reminders. This should be `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` to keep the deletion scoped correctly.

findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increment can race across concurrent cron invocations
findings.body: Both the success-path failure branch (line ~184) and the catch block (line ~195) update retryCount by computing `reminder.retryCount + 1` in application code from a value fetched earlier in the same request, rather than using Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }`. If the cron endpoint is invoked more than once concurrently (e.g. duplicate cron triggers, retried HTTP calls, multiple instances), two processes can read the same stale retryCount and write the same incremented value, losing an update. This means a reminder could fail many more than twice yet never reach retryCount > 1, defeating the intended cleanup logic and leaving broken reminders stuck in the scheduling loop indefinitely.

findings.title: Transient errors are treated the same as permanent failures, causing premature deletion of valid reminders
findings.body: Any error thrown while scheduling the SMS (network blip, Twilio rate limiting/outage, temporary API failure, etc.) increments retryCount exactly the same way as a permanent failure like an invalid phone number. Because the cron runs repeatedly and only allows 2 failures before the reminder is deleted (deleteMany with retryCount > 1), a short period of transient Twilio/network issues across two consecutive cron runs will cause legitimate, otherwise-valid workflow reminders to be permanently deleted before the scheduled date, even though the underlying booking/reminder was fine. There is no distinction between retryable and non-retryable errors, so the fix can silently drop reminders that should have eventually succeeded.

findings.title: Stale comment does not describe the new retryCount-based deletion
findings.body: The comment above the deleteMany call still reads "delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date", but the query now also deletes any reminder (regardless of method, see related finding) whose retryCount exceeds 1. The comment was not updated to describe this second deletion condition, which will mislead future maintainers reading only the comment about what rows are removed.

findings.title: No tests added for new retry/deletion behavior
findings.body: This PR introduces a behavioral change (failed SMS reminders are now deleted after two failures) that affects data integrity (permanent deletion of WorkflowReminder rows). No unit/integration tests were added to verify that retryCount increments correctly on failure, that reminders are deleted only after exceeding the retry threshold, or that successful sends are unaffected. Given the destructive nature of the deleteMany query, this logic should have test coverage to prevent regressions (e.g., accidental deletion of valid reminders or failure to ever clean up broken ones).
